_comment: ownRank = the SPEAKER's own Guild rank, same notation as rank (a named member of adventurers.json: they start at a set rank and rise with their level once they have travelled with the player, so a line that states their rank must say which); theirRank on a 'who' line compares it with the player's; ownPromoted = true: for a few days after the speaker's rank rose. A 'topic' may have several lines: they are tried in file order, so the ones with conditions go first. World awareness of the Adventurers Guild: greetings (Hello) from named NPCs and guards across the holds and Solstheim, built by tools/EspGen into AG_WorldDialogueQuest; INFO FormIDs are pinned in dialogue.ids.json under 'world:<id>' (voice files are named after them). Every line names the Adventurers Guild or an adventurer, never a bare 'Guild' (the Thieves Guild is right there in Riften). Fields: who = NPC editor ID, or guards = hold name / 'any' / 'retired'; status = unregistered | registered (default) | any; rank = 'E' exact, 'B+' at or above, 'E-C' inclusive range, '<B' below; promoted = the rank just reached (shown for a few days, see guild.json); chance = % of greetings that use the line when it applies; questDone / questNotDone = a quest editor ID the line waits for (or stops at) completion of. owner = 'sons' | 'notSons': whether the Stormcloaks hold Whiterun (the condition vanilla puts on Sinmir's own lines; he is captain of the guard under them). chance on a line overrides the table below for it. whileAlive / whenDead = an NPC editor ID that must be alive / dead; inFaction / notInFaction = a faction editor ID the speaker must (not) be in; liaison = true: only once this NPC keeps a Guild counter (a successor: Ysolda after Hulda). teammate = true/false: the speaker is (not) following the player; inParty = true/false: the speaker is (not) an active member of the player's adventuring party (AG_PartyMemberFaction, kept by the DLL). wanderers = true: any wandering adventurer (instead of who / guards), in every voice of wandererVoices; theirRank = 'above' | 'same' | 'below': the speaker's Guild rank against the player's. topic = a player line instead of a greeting: one per NPC (its records are numbered in tools/EspGen).
_wandererVoices: Wandering adventurers (adventurers.json 'wanderers'): the vanilla voice types their shared greetings are voiced in. One with any other voice (a mod's own) keeps the rank and says nothing of ours.

lines.text: Hulda says the Bannered Mare comes with the Adventurers Guild counter now. If I'm ever to buy it, I'll need the Guild's blessing as well as hers.
Hulda says you're one of the best adventurers on her books. Put in a good word for me when I buy the Mare?
Do you think the Adventurers Guild would certify a merchant? I keep a better ledger than half the adventurers who sign it.
Looking for work? The Adventurers Guild keeps its counter at the Bannered Mare. Hulda will take your name.
An adventurer, eh? Don't let the rank go to your head. The giants can't read.
The Adventurers Guild takes anyone with a sword and a dream. The Companions choose their own. There's a difference.
A ranked adventurer worth the name. Perhaps the Adventurers Guild does know how to judge a warrior. Occasionally.
Adventurers are all right. Good fighters, some of them. Almost as good as us.
S-rank? You should come spar with me. Vilkas says no, but Vilkas says no to everything.
You adventurers hunt for pay. We hunt for the hunt. Still, a pelt's a pelt.
The Adventurers Guild ranks you among its best hunters. I'd have said the same without any rank letter.
The Adventurers Guild does honest work, and you do it well. But Jorrvaskr stood long before the Guild, and will stand after.
I nearly became an adventurer before Jorrvaskr took me in. Don't tell Vilkas.
The Jarl's bounties still pay in gold, not Merit. Though I'm told the Adventurers Guild takes note of such things.
A top-ranked adventurer taking the Jarl's bounties. Balgruuf will be pleased. The treasury, less so.
Your adventurer's rank turns up in the reports I read. The Jarl prefers her problems solved by people with a record.
A rank like yours carries weight at the Blue Palace, adventurer. Use it wisely.
Adventurer? Corpulus keeps the Adventurers Guild counter at the Winking Skeever. Mind the Thalmor on your way.
The bards have run short of heroes to sing about. Adventurers like you might fix that.
Ulfric has little love for an Adventurers Guild that answers to no Jarl. He has less for trolls. Bring me proof and you'll be paid.
Ulfric noticed your adventurer's rank. That's rarely good news, but today it is.
Candlelight Hall keeps the Adventurers Guild counter. Elda will take your name, if not your excuses.
Heard a ranked adventurer cleared out a barrow near Kynesgrove. That you? Hm. Not bad.
In Riften, the Jarl pays her bounties in gold. The Adventurers Guild pays in Merit, and the Black-Briars pay in favors. Choose wisely.
An adventurer. Good for you. Keep your hands where I can see them anyway.
The Adventurers Guild? A guild with a ledger and no fence doesn't sound like much of a guild, lad.
One of the top-ranked adventurers, eh? With hands like yours, you're wasted on a ledger, lad.
The Silver-Bloods keep a close eye on the Adventurers Guild. Anyone with a rank and a sword interests them.
Thonar Silver-Blood asked your name today. A rank like yours makes the Silver-Bloods nervous.
Adventurer or not, you see nothing in Markarth. Understand?
Forsworn in the hills and work in the Silver-Blood Inn. Kleppr keeps the Adventurers Guild's book.
Falkreath's bounties usually end in the graveyard. Glad to see an adventurer who might come back.
The Adventurers Guild sent its best, then. Falkreath's graves will be emptier for it.
Dead Man's Drink keeps the Adventurers Guild counter. Fitting name, for that line of work.
Many adventurers pass through my garden eventually. Do try to be an exception.
The Jarl sees visions. I see missives. At least the Adventurers Guild's actually get done.
The Jarl dreamed of an adventurer walking out of the fog. I suppose you'll do.
Adventurer? Jonna at Moorside will want to see you. Plenty out in that fog needs killing.
Skald wants the giants off the mine roads. If the Adventurers Guild is sending help, send the strong ones.
An S-rank adventurer in Dawnstar. Skald will want to know why. So will the giants.
Nightmares every night, and adventurers every morning. At least your lot pays for their rooms.
Nights are quiet since the nightmares stopped. Adventurers still keep the inn busy, though.
Adventurers tip better than miners. They also ask for the same three songs. I've made my peace with it.
Same dream, every night, the whole town. If there's an adventurer who can do something about that, I'll stand them a drink.
Slept right through till morning. First time in months. Dawnstar can go back to its ordinary troubles, and those are adventurer's work too.
The Adventurers Guild rids Skyrim of its horrors one missive at a time. I think Mara approves.
The Jarl says Winterhold needs no adventurers. The Jarl says a great many things.
Even the Jarl called your rank impressive. From him, that's practically a feast day.
Two warm places in Winterhold: the College and the Frozen Hearth. The Adventurers Guild chose the one without mages.
Mages and adventurers aren't so different, you know. We both poke about in ruins we ought to leave alone.
Your adventurer's rank is quite remarkable. Have you considered the College? No? Pity.
Your adventurer's rank means little to House Redoran. Results, however, mean a great deal.
An S-rank adventurer from the mainland. House Redoran will want your name in its records too.
The Skaal need no rank letter to know who is strong. Still, your adventurer's rank sits well on you.
My father says you fight like the All-Maker's chosen. The Adventurers Guild must be running out of letters.
Another adventurer from the mainland. Stay out of the ash storms and away from the Bulwark's dead.
Came to Solstheim to earn your keep, outlander? The Adventurers Guild signs names at the Retching Netch. Ask for Geldis.
The Redoran Guard holds the wall. What lies beyond it is adventurer's work.
Ash in your boots, ash in your teeth. You'll stop noticing by the third day, adventurer. We all did.
Reavers along the coast, rieklings in the hills. Take your pick, adventurer. Nobody here will miss either.
A fresh guild card won't stop an ash spawn, adventurer. Neither will that look on your face.
Geldis signs anyone who can hold a pen. Holding a blade is the part we wait to see.
The last adventurer off the Northern Maiden went back on the next sailing. You're still here. On this island, that counts.
Captain Veleth read your name out at muster. He doesn't do that for outlanders.
House Redoran doesn't rank its warriors by letters. If it did, adventurer, I know where it would put you.
I've walked the Bulwark for years and never seen what you've seen. If the dead come over tonight, I'd sooner stand by you than the wall.
You carry a blade and no guild card. Geldis is ten paces that way, outlander. I prefer patrons the Adventurers Guild has heard of.
A guild card gets an adventurer through the door. It doesn't make them worth five hundred gold. I am.
My last patron outranked you, and he's dead in a bandit fort. Take that as advice, adventurer, not an insult.
We carry the same letter, you and I. The Adventurers Guild got one of us right.
You've climbed past me, outlander. Good. I've always charged more for working with the best.
An adventurer's work is the same as a sellsword's. The difference is that someone writes it down afterward.
I've had enough ash for one lifetime. If the Adventurers Guild has work on the mainland, I'm listening.
The Adventurers Guild raised my rank. Don't look so pleased with yourself. I did the fighting.
B-rank. Geldis put my name down the day the counter opened. A patron likes to see a letter before he opens his purse, so I let them think it matters.
A-rank, since we started travelling together. I'd say that was your doing, but I've a reputation as the best swordsman in Morrowind to think of.
I've a guild card somewhere under this armor. What's on it changes. What I charge doesn't.
My guards hold a wall. They can't leave it to chase what's out in the ash. An adventurer can, and I've stopped pretending we don't need that.
My men talk about you at the watch fires, adventurer. If you ever tire of working for coin, the Redoran Guard pays worse and asks more.
I put the Adventurers Guild's license on Geldis's bar myself. The Councilor signed it the morning after the ash spawn reached the Bulwark.
Raven Rock has been a struggle to hold, adventurer. It is somewhat less of one since your kind arrived. I'll admit that much.
I've been in one guild already, and it didn't hand out cards. Yours pays in the open. Takes some getting used to.
Adventurers are the best thing to happen to a smith. You lot dent everything you own. Bring it by.
I've carried more guild cards across the Sea of Ghosts this year than sacks of grain. Not as many on the way back, mind.
I can pick out an adventurer before they've paid the fare. Twenty years on the Northern Maiden will do that. It's the boots.
My goodness, an adventurer. If your work takes you beyond the Bulwark, I'd pay well for netch jelly. I daren't go out there myself.
You've been out past the Bulwark and come back whole, more than once. I do hope the Adventurers Guild knows what it has in you.
The East Empire Company left, and the Adventurers Guild came. It's not the trade I was hoping for, but an adventurer still needs rope and lamp oil.
Whatever you find out in the ash, bring it here before you take it to the mainland. I pay fair, and I pay today.
My great-grandfather went into ruins all over Tamriel. No guild behind him, no card in his pocket. Mark my words, adventurer. It's not the letter that brings you home.
In and out of every hole on this island, you adventurers. And not one of you can read a seam of rock.
Adventurers Guild, eh? Then you've coin coming in. When it stops, and it always stops, you'll come looking for me.
You've got a name on this island now. Names don't scare me. Debts are what I collect, adventurer.
I watch you adventurers walk into the Netch like it's nothing. Geldis won't have me through the door. Spare a coin, sera?
I pulled more ebony out of this rock than any adventurer ever pulled out of a tomb. Nobody gave me a letter for it.
The Skaal keep no guild. What one of us cannot do alone, the village does together. Your Adventurers Guild seems to me a village that walks.
I have heard the dark elves of Raven Rock speak your name, adventurer. They do not praise outsiders easily. Neither do we.
Your Adventurers Guild gives a letter to each who serves it. The All-Maker gives no letters. He sends the winter, and we see who is standing in spring.
The land speaks of those who walk it, adventurer. Of you it speaks without fear. That is rarer than any rank.
An adventurer hunts for coin. The Skaal hunt for need. Ask yourself before each kill which of the two you are doing. Then you will be welcome at our fires.
I have seen your kind carry pelts and claws back to Raven Rock for the Adventurers Guild. Take what they ask for and no more. The beast gave it. It was not yours.
Blades from the mainland come to my forge chipped by ash spawn and rieklings. Your Adventurers Guild keeps a smith busy, outsider.
A warrior of your standing should carry better steel than that, adventurer. On the mainland they forge for coin. Here we forge for the one who will hold it.
I'm no adventurer, as I tell everyone. But I've begun to wish the Adventurers Guild kept a counter up here. I'd be its best customer.
Every ruin on this island wants a scholar to read it and an adventurer to walk in first. I know which of the two I am.
Is it true the Adventurers Guild takes anyone with the nerve? Even a Skaal? I am only asking. Do not tell my mother I asked.
They say you carry a rank from the Adventurers Guild. In three or four winters I mean to carry one too. Wulf says I must learn patience first.
Thirsk has no ranks and no cards. You win your place with an axe, or you don't have one. Still, adventurer, I've seen worse ways of sorting the strong from the soft.
They say the Adventurers Guild puts you near the top of its list. Good. I'd rather drink beside someone who earned it than a hall full of horker-brains.
Warriors in the wild, living like the Nords of old. That was Thirsk. Your Adventurers Guild comes closer to it than most things on the mainland.
An adventurer who lives long enough to earn a rank has learned how to take a blow. Most learn it the hard way. I can teach it quicker.
Master Neloth says adventurers fetch the things he can't be bothered to fetch. He says the same about apprentices.
I asked Master Neloth whether I could register with the Adventurers Guild. He laughed for quite a long time. I'm still not sure what the answer was.
Is this what adventurers do all day? It's terrifying. It's also much better than scrubbing out Master Neloth's cauldrons.
The Adventurers Guild sent a runner asking after you again. I told him the Thane keeps their own hours.
I am sworn to carry your burdens. The Adventurers Guild says I get credit for it now. That's new.
Hulda says they talk about you at the Bannered Mare. I pretend I'm not proud. It isn't working.
Proudspire is quiet without you. I've been reading the Adventurers Guild postings at the Winking Skeever, just to keep sharp.
A housecarl and an adventurer, both at once. My mother would say pick one. I'd rather not.
They know your name at the Blue Palace and at the Winking Skeever. I get asked about you in both. I say very little.
Hjerim's secure, my Thane. I hear there's work at the Adventurers Guild counter, if you're restless.
I've stood guard on a doorstep most of my life. Walking into the trouble with you makes a change.
Windhelm respects a strong arm. An adventurer's card says you've got one. Simple enough.
Honeyside is in order. In this city, that takes a housecarl standing in the doorway. Go and do your adventuring.
Riften taught me to watch people's hands. It has kept one adventurer alive so far. Now it's keeping two.
The Bee and Barb keeps an honest counter for the Adventurers Guild. In Riften, I don't say that about much.
Vlindrel Hall's safe. Nothing gets past me. Nothing's tried, mind. Markarth saves its knives for the streets.
They call me the Bulwark. Standing in front of an adventurer is the same work as standing in front of a door. More walking.
The Reach eats adventurers. Forsworn in every pass. Good thing you've got a wall of your own.
The estate is quiet. Wolves, a bandit or two, nothing my scimitars couldn't settle. Adventurer's work, done at the door.
My father rode with the Alik'r. He'd have understood the Adventurers Guild. Coin for a blade, and no questions about your banner.
A great many adventurers are buried in Falkreath. I intend to see that you are not one of them.
All's well at the hall. The giants keep to their camps and I keep to the walls. I leave the rest to the adventurers. To you, I mean.
A housecarl guards with his life. Nobody said how far from the house. I've stopped counting the miles.
Dawnstar's inn has an Adventurers Guild counter now. The miners trust it more than they trust the Jarl. Don't repeat that.
The marsh has been quiet. Too quiet, for Hjaalmarch. If the Adventurers Guild posts anything from Morthal, I'd take it seriously.
Steel in one hand, a spell in the other. The Adventurers Guild has no box for that on its card. I checked.
I've warded the manor twice this month. Something in the fog keeps testing it. That will be adventurer's work, sooner or later.
Adventurers come through Dragonsreach every week. Most want a bounty and a look at the Jarl. I watch their hands, not their cards.
The Adventurers Guild vouches for you. I don't take anyone's word. But I've seen your work, and that I'll take.
The Adventurers Guild keeps its counter down at the Skeever, and its people out of the Blue Palace. I like that arrangement.
You want to impress the Jarl? Do the work the Adventurers Guild posts. She hears about it. I make sure of that.
An adventurer in Riften with clean hands. Keep them that way and we'll have no quarrel.
My family has fought for Skyrim since the first Snow-Shod. I know what earned rank looks like. Yours is earned.
Forsworn on the roads and Silver-Bloods in the keep. If the Adventurers Guild thins out either, I'll not complain.
State your business with the Jarl plainly. Adventurers usually do. It's the one thing I like about them.
The Jarl leaves the hold's troubles to others. These days that means me, and the Adventurers Guild.
Falkreath's roads are safer than they were. I'd thank the Adventurers Guild, if I knew who to thank. I suppose it's you.
Morthal needs strong hands, not visions. The Adventurers Guild at least sends hands.
If you've taken a missive in Hjaalmarch, bring word to me as well as the inn. Someone here should know what's out in that marsh.
I've carried more mead to adventurers at the Bannered Mare than to anyone. They tip like they might not be back.
Do your jobs, take your coin, and stay out of Black-Briar business. That's free advice, adventurer. The next lot costs.
I trained at the Bards College. Nobody writes songs about the Adventurers Guild. The work's too honest. Honest doesn't rhyme with much.
The Legion taught me to respect anyone who walks toward the noise. Adventurers do. Most of Dawnstar doesn't.
Kraldar says the Adventurers Guild's counter is the first new thing in Winterhold since the Collapse. He means it kindly.
I'm too old for adventuring and too stubborn to say so. If the Adventurers Guild wants an old soldier's advice, it knows where I drink.
Whiterun has room for anyone who earns their keep, adventurer. My guards sleep easier since the Adventurers Guild set up at the Bannered Mare.
An adventurer! Riften is fortunate. My steward tells me the Adventurers Guild is quite orderly. I do so like things orderly.
The Reach bleeds from a hundred small cuts. My soldiers can't be everywhere. If the Adventurers Guild closes a few of them, it has my thanks.
Ah, an adventurer. Splendid. That's one more problem I needn't get out of this chair for.
The Adventurers Guild takes no side in the war, they tell me. I don't trust a blade with no side. But it kills giants, so I'll bear it.
At last, someone in Winterhold who isn't wearing a robe. The Adventurers Guild is welcome here. More welcome than some.
I swung an axe with the Companions before your Adventurers Guild had a counter to lean on. Still. Work is work, and you lot do it.
The Adventurers Guild rents its counter under a Silver-Blood roof. Remember whose roof, and we'll get on fine.
Dawnstar's a mining town with a soldier's problems. I served the Legion long enough to know good irregulars when I see them, adventurer.
I run a mine. I know what it costs when the roads close. Every missive an adventurer finishes is ore that reaches the docks.
We have the College, the inn, and now the Adventurers Guild's counter. That's three reasons to visit Winterhold. It used to be one.
The Adventurers Guild asks only what you can do. Nord, elf or Argonian. Windhelm could learn from that.
Vignar pulled me out of the gutter once. I've a soft spot for anyone doing honest work for coin. That's your Adventurers Guild, near enough.
Mother tolerates the Adventurers Guild. You should understand how rare that is, and how quickly it can change.
The Adventurers Guild pays its rent on the day it's due. In Markarth, that makes it the Silver-Bloods' favorite lodger.
Oh! An adventurer. Dengeir says I'm not to talk to strangers. But he says you lot are useful, so perhaps that's all right.
Stonehills sends its troubles to the Adventurers Guild counter in Morthal. It's cheaper than losing a week's ore to bandits.
I've crewed ships with worse discipline than your Adventurers Guild. A posted job, a fair share, and everyone knows their rank.
So the Adventurers Guild writes your name in a book and gives you a letter. I slept through a few things. I'm not sure I'd have invented that one.
You realize I'm traveling under your guild card now. A vampire, in an honest trade. My mother would be appalled.
Do they have a rank for someone a few thousand years late to register? No? Pity.
Go on, then. Go and be an adventurer. I'll be here when the job turns out stranger than it sounded. They always do.
Most of the Dwemer gyros I've studied were carried out of a ruin by some adventurer who thought they were scrap. Bless every one of them.
If the Adventurers Guild ever wants crossbows, send them to me. Isran will say no. I'll say bring gold.
I was a Vigilant before this. We hunted daedra and asked nothing. The Adventurers Guild asks a fee and gets more done. I've stopped judging.
The Dawnguard hunts one thing. You hunt whatever's posted. It keeps a man from getting stale.
Adventurers kill for coin. I kill vampires for what they took. But a dead vampire is a dead vampire. I don't ask who's paying.
Good. A real fight. The Adventurers Guild picks them better than I expected.
I nearly signed with the Adventurers Guild as an E-rank, same as anyone starting out. Then I heard about the Dawnguard, and here I am.
Is it always like this with you? I mean, it's fine. I'm fine. I just want to know if it's always like this.
I gave my guild card back the day I came to Isran. Some days I miss it. A missive never asked me to stand watch in the rain.
I've been on the wrong end of an Adventurers Guild missive. Don't ask. I'm on the right end of things now.
The Adventurers Guild posts bounties on my kind. I've read a few. The descriptions are insulting, and the prices are worse.
An adventurer's rank. How charming. Mortals do love to be told where they stand.
Rank you earn with a blade, I understand. It's the one thing your Adventurers Guild and this court agree on.
They say the Adventurers Guild takes anyone who pays the fee. Anyone. I've wondered about it. Don't tell Feran.
Adventurers bring me the best steel I've ever worked. They don't bring it willingly, mind.
Adventurers. Sellswords with paperwork. Still, you people go where the trouble is, and that's more than I can say for the Jarls.
I asked about you. The Adventurers Guild keeps better records than the Vigil ever did. You'll do.
You're with the Adventurers Guild too? Good. Then you know how this goes. Help me put this bear down, and we'll talk.
I still carry my guild card. Isran grumbles about it. I tell him a troll doesn't care which book my name's in.
Arkay says the Adventurers Guild does good work. Well, he says it's adequate. He's a hard god to impress.
An order that writes everything down and ranks its members by merit. I approve, adventurer. The Moth Priests would call that a promising start.
Serana tells me mortals now keep a guild for people who walk into ruins on purpose. In my day we called that a shortage of sense.
A guild of adventurers. Every age has one. I have outlived a dozen of them, and I remember none of their names.
I have read the Adventurers Guild's missives. Tidy, brief, and paid on completion. Our court could learn something from that. I won't say so aloud.
You fight for a guild. I fight for this court. Come down to the yard sometime, and we'll see which of us learned more.
E-rank adventurer, is it? Everyone starts somewhere. Usually somewhere with rats.
New to the Adventurers Guild? Stick to skeevers and wolves for a while.
Don't go picking fights above your rank. The Adventurers Guild won't pay for your funeral.
A C-rank adventurer. That's where the real work starts. And the real graves.
A C-rank adventurer in town. Try not to start anything we'll have to finish.
B-rank? The Adventurers Guild doesn't hand those out for killing skeevers.
You've got that look. Veteran of too many barrows.
If there's trouble tonight, I'll know which adventurer to call.
An S-rank adventurer. By the Nine... I didn't think there were any left in Skyrim.
My captain says an S-rank is worth a whole garrison. Don't prove him right tonight.
Stand aside, it's the Adventurers Guild's S-rank. Sorry. Carry on.
I used to be an adventurer like you. Then I took an arrow in the knee.
Still carry my old Adventurers Guild card. Doesn't open many doors anymore.
I was a ranked adventurer once. You've gone further than I ever did. Good on you.
Sixteen years with the Adventurers Guild and I never saw an S-rank. Now one's walking my beat.
Used to be a dozen adventurers drinking at the inn every night. The war took most of them.
Adventurers keep going missing lately. Watch yourself, and watch what you say around the Thalmor.
Heard you're a D-rank adventurer now. Not a greenhorn anymore, then.
Word is you made C-rank. The barracks had a wager on it.
B-rank, they're saying. The whole hold's talking about you.
An A-rank adventurer! I'll be telling my children I saw you walk by.
An S-rank adventurer. Even the Jarl's court is talking. Mind the bards, they'll want a song.
A real adventurer, here in the Blue Palace! I've polished a hundred silver platters dreaming of a day like this. Tell me you've come to carry me off on some grand adventure!
They say you're one of the finest adventurers in all of Skyrim. And here you are... I've been waiting for you...
An adventurer. How quaint. I suppose someone has to do the Adventurers Guild's dirty work. Do wipe your boots before you come near me.
Ah, the famous adventurer! I've told the Jarl we simply must have you up to the Cloud District. My idea, naturally.
Adventurers! My favorite customers. You come in with gold, you leave with my wares, and everyone's happy. Well, I'm happy.
The Adventurers Guild buys your trophies now, I hear. Stealing my business! Still, for my favorite adventurer, I might knock off a septim. Might.
An adventurer! Talos too began with nothing but a sword and a road. Stay, and hear how he became a god!
Behold! A hero of the Adventurers Guild stands before us! Talos walks in the deeds of such as these!
M'aiq hears the Adventurers Guild gives out letters instead of numbers. M'aiq prefers numbers. Letters are too easy to lie about.
M'aiq was an S-rank adventurer once. The Adventurers Guild lost the paperwork. M'aiq has forgiven them.
Solitude is grateful to the Adventurers Guild. Every road you make safe is one less widow in Haafingar.
They speak of you at court, adventurer. Torygg would have liked you, I think. He always admired those who stood up to danger.
Warriors come through court every day. An adventurer who actually finishes the job? That's rarer.
Half the court wants to hire you, adventurer. The other half is afraid to. That's how you know you're doing well.
I hear you're an adventurer now. Well, I'll be keeping my eye on you. Somebody in this city has to.
Everyone's talking about you, adventurer! Well, I'm talking about you, and I talk to everyone.
An adventurer. Good. Skyrim needs strong arms, whatever letter the Adventurers Guild writes beside your name.
Your name reaches even the Palace of the Kings, adventurer. Skyrim remembers those who stand tall. See that you stand with her.
An adventurer! You wouldn't happen to be clearing Dwemer ruins? Do be careful with the artifacts. Some of us have studied them for decades.
Every Dwemer ruin a famous adventurer clears is one I should have catalogued first. Still... I would pay handsomely for your notes.
An adventurer, sniffing around Markarth. The Reach has a long memory. Mind what you uncover.
Even in the Reach, they say your name, adventurer. Some with awe. Some with a knife behind their back. Remember that.
An adventurer with ambition. I like ambition. It's so easy to put a price on.
The Adventurers Guild thinks very highly of you. So do I. Come see me when you're ready to work for someone who pays better.
Well, look at you, a real adventurer. Dibella teaches us to appreciate beauty. And you're... well, rugged.
The famous adventurer, in my bunkhouse! Dibella must be smiling on me. Stay a while, why don't you?
I have seen you in my visions, adventurer. A letter burning brighter beside your name. Be about your business. It is not finished.
My visions showed me a great adventurer walking into this hall. And here you stand. Mind that you do not fall as fast as you rose.
An adventurer! Just who I hoped to see. You wouldn't come across any Mythic Dawn relics on your travels, would you?
A famous adventurer, visiting my humble museum! You simply must sign the guestbook. It'll do wonders for business.
Adventurers Guild, eh? A ledger with everyone's name in it. Just the sort of thing the Empire would love to get its hands on.
They say you're the finest adventurer in the hold. I'd wager my nephew Siddgeir's already trying to buy you. Don't let him.
An adventurer, in my library. Don't mistake the Adventurers Guild's ledger for reading material. Look around. Learn something.
Everyone knows your name now, adventurer. Bring me a book from one of those ruins you're famous for, and I might remember it too.
An adventurer, huh? I used to be an adventurer, y'know. Then I... well. Then I found the Frozen Hearth.
The finest adventurer in Skyrim, drinking right here! Buy me one, would you? For old times' sake.
An adventurer. How quaint. If the Adventurers Guild can teach you to fetch things properly, you may yet be of use to me.
Ah, the famous adventurer. The Adventurers Guild must be very proud. I, of course, am merely mildly impressed. Don't let it go to your head.
You've the look of someone hunting for work. The Adventurers Guild takes names at the bar. Try not to embarrass the rest of us.
E-rank? I've scraped tougher things than you off my boots. Come back when your guild card means something.
D-rank. So you can kill a wolf without help. The Adventurers Guild must be thrilled.
Fresh ink on your guild card and already strutting. The missive board will cure you of that.
C-rank, same as me. Don't think that makes us equals. I earned mine before the war thinned the ranks.
Another C-rank adventurer in Whiterun. Stay off the good missives and we'll get along.
B-rank. Hulda's ledger must be getting generous.
An A-rank adventurer, drinking where I drink. Suppose I'll have to stop calling myself the best blade in this hall.
S-rank. Shor's bones. I'd heard there were none left. I'd be honored to buy you a drink.
Took a missive out past the western watchtower. Bandits. The guards had walked right by them for a week.
A guard gets paid to stand at a gate. An adventurer gets paid when the job's done. That's the difference.
I've a missive waiting and a mug to finish. In that order, once the mug's done.
Made C-rank, did you? Took you long enough. Welcome to real work.
B-rank already? Luck. Has to be luck.
C-rank, and I'd be higher if Hulda's ledger counted every bandit I've dropped. Someone has to do what the guards won't.
Commander of the guard now. The Adventurers Guild set my name aside for it. Their loss, Whiterun's gain.
I was a C-rank adventurer before I took the watch. These guards will learn to work like one.
Keep your missives outside the walls, adventurer. Inside them, you answer to me.
If the watch had three blades like yours I'd sleep at night. Don't tell the men I said that.
The Bannered Mare is mine now, and the Adventurers Guild's counter with it. Best purchase I ever made.
Mikael can keep the Bannered Mare. The Adventurers Guild's counter is mine, and it's the half that turns a profit.
The old man's gone, so the Winking Skeever's mine. The Adventurers Guild's counter came with it. Lucky me.
Candlehearth Hall's mine to keep now, and the Adventurers Guild's counter with it. Never thought I'd see the day.
The Bee and Barb is mine to tend now, and the Adventurers Guild's counter with it. I would trade both to have her back.
You fight for coin? Then sign with the Adventurers Guild. They don't care who you were, only what you can kill.
Fresh guild card? Don't wave it at me. Come back when you've buried something bigger than a wolf.
D-rank, same as me. Good. Maybe now someone in this city can keep up.
You outrank me now. Hm. Buy me a drink and tell me how you did it.
An S-rank. The Companions would beg to have you. Let them beg.
The Companions wouldn't have me. The Adventurers Guild asked one question: can you fight? I can fight.
Sinmir's a rank above me and never lets me forget it. Ask him when he last turned in a missive.
They made you D-rank. About time I had some competition.
D-rank. I took my blade there after Jorrvaskr shut its doors on me. The Guild pays, and it doesn't ask for my life story.
They read my name out at the Bannered Mare. I'd have got there alone. Not this fast, though.
I stand level with Sinmir now. He's stopped mentioning rank. Funny, that.
Same letter on both our cards again. I mean to keep it that way, so don't get ahead of yourself.
C-rank now. Took walking half of Skyrim with you to get it. I'd be honored to walk the other half fighting by your side.
I carry a guild card, and the letter on it is my business. Ask me what I've killed instead.
If you can hold a blade, register with the Adventurers Guild. Skyrim needs people who run toward trouble.
Every adventurer starts at the bottom of the ledger. Keep your word, finish your missives, and the rank will come.
I've heard your name at the Bee and Barb. You're making a difference. Don't stop.
B-rank. Then we stand level, you and I. It's been a long time since I could say that to anyone.
A-rank. You've gone further than I ever did. I'm glad it was you.
S-rank. I chased that seal across half of Tamriel and never came close. Wear it well.
I was a B-rank adventurer before a Dwemer ruin nearly finished me. These days I take one job only: Riften.
The Adventurers Guild's work is honest. In this city, that makes its counter the cleanest table in the Bee and Barb.
Word of your promotion reached Riften before you did. Well earned.
Word of your promotion reached Riften before you did. Well earned.
B-rank, though I've not taken a missive in years after losing my blade and nearly my life. The Guild keeps my name on the books all the same and I'm proud to be a member.
The Adventurers Guild has raised my rank. I had made my peace with never seeing that happen.
A-rank. I thought my climbing was done the day I lost Grimsever. Travelling with you proved me wrong.
The letter on my guild card matters less than what I do with it. Riften taught me that.
A traveler with a blade should carry a guild card. The Adventurers Guild keeps a counter in every hold capital.
New to the Adventurers Guild? Learn the land before you learn the blade. Most adventurers who die, die lost.
You've the look of someone who's been past the end of the road. I miss that. Tell me where you've been.
I was a D-rank scout for the Adventurers Guild before I married. Verner thinks I've given it up. I've only stopped telling him.
I found the vein this mine sits on while I was out on a Guild job. Best missive I never finished.
I still carry my guild card. D-rank. I tell myself I'll take one more missive when the season turns.
The Adventurers Guild moved me up a rank. I'd forgotten how good that feels.
C-rank, would you believe it. Verner thinks I've been picking snowberries. I've been out past the end of the road with you.
I carry a guild card again, and I mean to keep earning it. That's all a letter is for.
One day I'm going to register with the Adventurers Guild. I've already practiced signing my name.
Is that a guild card? A real one? What rank are you? No, don't tell me. I want to guess.
A B-rank adventurer? Here, in Rorikstead? Nobody's going to believe me.
An A-rank? In Rorikstead? I've only ever heard of A-ranks in songs.
S-rank. You're... I thought those were made up. Can I see your guild card? Just for a moment?
I've got the armor and I've got the name. All I need now is a guild card. Take me along and I'll earn one.
I'm in a real adventuring party. Me! I keep reading my guild card to make sure it still says so.
On the road without a guild card? The Adventurers Guild takes names at any hold capital's inn.
Keep at it. The first few ranks are the hardest.
I remember my first missive. Barely. Stay on the road until your guild card's seen some weather.
Same rank, by the look of you. May your missives pay better than mine.
Another adventurer on the road. If you're after the same job, I saw it first.
That's a rank I've only seen in a ledger. Safe roads, adventurer.
You're the one they talk about at the counter. An honor.
Can't stop. The Adventurers Guild doesn't pay me to stand around.
